title: BTT SKR Pico (RP2040, USB)
description: BIGTREETECH SKR Pico v1.0: RP2040, USB serial, no bootloader, W25Q080 flash chip. Flash by copying a .uf2 to the RPI-RP2 drive.
dda_note: RP2040 runs Klipper at a 12 MHz timer clock (CLOCK_FREQ from the built .config). 40 kHz DDA = 300 clock ticks per tick; max 20,000 steps/s per axis (2*|steps| <= n), i.e. 250 mm/s at 80 steps/mm. ISR cost is unmeasured.
serial_usb: USB CDC-ACM serial (appears as /dev/serial/by-id/usb-Klipper_rp2040_*). Baud setting is ignored for USB; hosts usually still pass 250000.
notes: Compile-only: built in a sandbox with Klipper v0.13.0; never flashed or run on this board by the author.
BOOTSEL: hold the boot button while plugging USB in (or tap RESET while holding it); a drive named RPI-RP2 appears.
UNVERIFIED: whether your particular SKR Pico revision has a W25Q080 flash chip; this follows Klipper's own SKR Pico config header and defaults.

build_sizes.note: Klipper v0.13.0, arm-none-eabi/avr gcc from Ubuntu apt, sandbox build. RAM = static data+bss only; the segment queue itself is allocated at run time (depth * sizeof(segment): 24 bytes ARM, 23 bytes AVR).

sources: Klipper v0.13.0 config/generic-bigtreetech-skr-pico-v1.0.cfg (header comments: RP2040, USB, copy out/klipper.uf2 in boot mode)
